name: Meltmaxxing

lead: Meltmaxxing is a joke format that borrows the look of looksmaxxing edits. Instead of showing a sharpened jawline, the person tucks in their chin and makes an ugly face, 'maxxing' toward looking worse.

It does not aim to improve appearance. Its connection to the wiki's topic is as commentary: it is a way users poke fun at the style of looksmaxxing content, and it shows how the vocabulary of the community spread into mainstream meme culture.

paras: Creators reuse the music, sound effects and visual style of looksmaxxing edits but show themselves 'meltmaxxing' instead. It is done for humor in short videos.
No physical risk is reported; it is a pose for a video. The trend's main significance is cultural.

angle.text: Meltmaxxing is not a method for looking better. It is satire of looksmaxxing content, and it is documented here as part of the community's wider cultural footprint.

lead: Meltmaxxing is an ironic meme and 'maxxing' slang term inspired by the TikToker Cookie King and by the looksmaxxing community. In the videos, a person tucks the chin in and pulls an unattractive face, satirizing looksmaxxing clips.[1]

It began in May 2025, with early examples posted on TikTok on May 14 and Instagram on May 29. Cookie King's main TikTok account was banned in June 2025.[1] Other users copied the sounds and visual effects of looksmaxxing edits to show themselves 'meltmaxxing', and several clips drew hundreds of thousands of plays between May and July 2025.[1]

paras: Know Your Meme traces meltmaxxing to Cookie King, who posted videos in May 2025 in which he tucked in his chin and made an ugly face to satirize looksmaxxing videos.[1] Imitations followed: a May 27 clip passed 400,000 plays, a June 21 clip also passed 400,000, and a July 2 clip using a 'Men Men Men' sound effect reworded as 'Melt Melt Melt' passed 500,000.[1] The meme also appeared in other settings, such as a clip of an audience member doing it during an MMA question-and-answer session in June.[1]

Looksmaxxing is an online practice aimed at maximizing physical attractiveness, which spread from forums to TikTok in the 2020s.[2] Meltmaxxing reuses its 'maxxing' naming convention and its video style as a joke, and the Know Your Meme entry describes it as drawing on the community.[1][2]

timeline.event: Cookie King posts early meltmaxxing videos in mid-May; a main account is banned in June.[1]
Imitation clips spread through July, some exceeding 400,000 plays.[1]
